transcript: International icon and cartoon character Betty Boop now has her own Broadway show, and it was a bit of a mixed bag for me. Now, I attended the second preview, so things can and will change, but the key elements of the show seem pretty set and the marketing tells you what you're getting into. Let's start with the good stuff. Jasmine Amy Rogers is amazing as Betty Boop. It's really exciting to see someone in complete control of their craft, and she is without a doubt a triple threat. The music is good, it's not super memorable, but it's got some bops and stylistically, it's perfect for this show — reminded me a bit of Some Like It Hot. Another similarity to that show is the choreo being super tight and the ensemble being absolutely locked in. For a second preview, I was kind of blown away by how crisp it was. I was not as blown away by the plot, which initially seemed promising, but didn't really end up going anywhere interesting for me. There’s like a lot of side characters that don't really have time to properly earn the audience's investment, and honestly, anytime that Jasmine Amy Rogers wasn't on stage, I was just waiting for her to come back. That’s partially a testament to how magnetic of a performance she is giving, but I also wanted more depth and focus on her journey specifically, as she is the title character. The book scenes that didn't involve Betty felt a little long, and the somewhat pandering script doesn't really feel as slick and campy as I'd hoped it would for a show that's based on a cartoon character. But, if you're looking for a fun Broadway musical that brings the nostalgia factor, this definitely fits the bill. Boop! is at its best when it's big, bold, and theatrical, and in fairness, there are a lot of fun design surprises to appreciate here, such as a colorful costume trick at the top of Act 2. With that, another playbill for my collection.
